section.title: Situation
section.p: We have one live system. When we develop — writing code, running migrations, testing changes — we do it on the same instance that is actively receiving Telegram messages, running agent cycles, and storing chat history. Every mix ecto.migrate is a live deploy. Every recompile touches the production supervision tree. This has worked, but it means we cannot confidently test anything without risking the running system.
We want a staging environment so that code changes, migrations, and new features can be exercised before they hit production.

section.title: Core Idea
section.p: Two separate git checkouts on the same machine. Not worktrees — full independent clones. Each checkout gets its own Postgres database. The staging instance must not listen to the production Telegram chat. Everything else is negotiable.
The three isolation boundaries that matter:

item.p: Git. Separate clones mean separate branches, separate HEAD, separate working trees. You cannot corrupt production's checkout from staging. Worktrees share the .git directory and can interfere with each other, which is why we avoid them.
Postgres. Separate databases. Migrations run independently. You can drop and recreate the staging database at any time. A bad migration in staging does not touch production data.

Telegram. This is the hard boundary. If both instances listen to the same group chat, messages get processed twice and the group receives duplicate responses. Staging must either disable Telegram entirely or use a separate bot account talking to a separate test chat.

section.title: Observations and Considerations
section.p: Some things I noticed while looking at the codebase that are relevant to whoever implements this:

The runtime configuration in config/runtime.exs is already well-factored around environment variables — DATABASE_URL, PORT, PHX_HOST, SECRET_KEY_BASE. Staging can be configured entirely through a different env file without code changes. The bot startup path in Froth.Telegram.Bots reads from application config; adding a kill switch that prevents any bot workers from starting would be a small change and would be the simplest way to keep staging silent on Telegram.

There is a FROTH_NODE_ROLE variable that already distinguishes "full" nodes from "worker" nodes. Staging could be modeled as a third role, or it could just be a full node with Telegram disabled — whichever feels cleaner.

External API keys (Anthropic, Replicate, Gemini, xAI) are stateless and safe to share between environments. A staging call to Claude does not affect a production call. The isolation boundary is Telegram and Postgres, not the LLM providers.

The main value is migration safety. Destructive migrations — dropping columns, renaming tables — are the ones where staging pays for itself. The telemetry_events to events rename in RFC-0008 was tested by Codex's test suite, but a staging database running the full application would have caught any runtime references the tests missed.

Staging does not need to run continuously. It can be started when someone is actively developing and shut down otherwise. Whether it also wants a systemd unit for convenience is a decision that can be made later.

If we eventually want staging to exercise the full agent loop (not just the web layer), we would create a test bot via BotFather, add it to a test group chat, and point the staging instance at that bot token. This is optional and can be deferred.

section.title: What This Does Not Solve
section.p: This is about code and data isolation during development. It does not address blue-green deployment, zero-downtime production restarts, automatic data seeding from production, or shared external state (both environments hit the same Replicate and Anthropic accounts, so a staging image generation still costs money). These are all real concerns but separate from the immediate goal of "let me test a migration without holding my breath."

section.title: Workflow Sketch
section.p: The broad shape of how this gets used: the developer works in the staging checkout, makes changes, runs migrations, starts the server, verifies things work. When confident, merges to main. Switches to the production checkout, pulls, migrates, restarts. Codex dispatches follow the same pattern — Codex commits to a branch, the branch gets tested in staging before merging to production.

The details of how the env file is structured, what the startup script looks like, which port staging runs on — these are implementation decisions that should be made by whoever sets it up, not prescribed here.

section.title: Implementation Status
section.p: As of 2026-07-25, this RFC is partially implemented.

config/runtime.exs supports environment-driven node roles, database URLs, ports, hosts, secrets, and Telegram bot autostart control. The local full-node workflow also demonstrates that Froth can boot with clustering and bot side effects disabled.
Froth does not yet have a dedicated staging checkout, staging database workflow, test bot identity, service definition, or staging-specific operational workflow.
